subject: Clarify storage & retention for prompt inputs and generated outputs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@helixmed.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on prompt/output storage

Hi Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few clarifying questions so we can get you a concise security and retention answer packet:

Summary from call:
- Helix will send clinical text (patient name, MRN, partial DOB) plus clinician notes to Redwood for real-time summarization and reranking.
- Priority: minimize retention of PHI; provide audit logs for access; ensure data residency in US only.
- Potential deployment paths discussed: Hosted API (fast), Dedicated GPU pool (reserved), Private (VPC/on-prem).

Clarifying questions (can you confirm the items below?):
1) Which specific fields in the prompts are considered PHI for Helix? (e.g., full name, MRN, full DOB, address)
2) Desired retention window for prompt inputs and generation outputs (examples: 0 days / 30 days / 90 days)?
3) Is the requirement that outputs are never used for model training (strict opt-out) or is a 30-day non-training window acceptable?
4) Preferred data residency region (US-East, US-West, EU)?
5) Any vendor-specific KMS/BYOK requirements?

Next steps from our side: we will pull the short "data flow & retention" one-pager and a draft SLA showing configurable retention flags. I've attached a short diagram (redwood-prompt-data-flow.pdf) and will follow up with a draft SLA for Helix.

If you can confirm 1–4 above (or reply with any additional constraints), we’ll loop in our security lead and provide a consolidated statement you can share with your SecOps team.

Proposed timeline: confirmation by 6/12 -> security packet to you by 6/15.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-prompt-data-flow.pdf
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@helixmed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: SecurityOps <sec-ops@helixmed.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on prompt/output storage

Thanks, Soojin — good recap. Answers inline below:

1) PHI fields: patient full name (sometimes initials only), MRN, partial DOB (YYYY-MM), clinical ID tokens. We also sometimes pass small device identifiers.
2) Retention window: Helix requirement is MAX 30 days for both prompts and outputs on hosted services. For production (if we go Private/Dedicated) preference is 0 days retention for prompts & outputs.
3) Training: Helix MUST have assurance that Helix data is not used to train Redwood public models. We expect a contractual opt-out.
4) Data residency: US-only; US-East preferred (Virginia).
5) KMS: We prefer BYOK but can accept Redwood-managed keys if we have role-separated access and clear audit logs.

SecurityOps is on cc and will follow with technical specifics. Can you confirm whether Redwood’s hosted API supports a 30-day max retention setting and an explicit no-training contractual clause? Also confirm where access logs are stored and the log format (JSON/CSV) and retention.

If possible, schedule a quick 30-min call with your security lead next week — our SecOps would like to run through the checklist.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, Helix Medical Software
alex.morgan@helixmed.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@helixmed.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on prompt/output storage

Alex — appreciate the clear answers. Below are direct responses to each item and next steps. I’ll put our security lead on a follow-up with SecOps once you confirm availability. Attached: draft SLA and data-flow diagram.

Summary answers (short):
- Retention: Redwood hosted API defaults to temporary retention used for abuse detection, debugging, and quality; default window is up to 30 days but is configurable. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support configurable retention down to 0 days for both prompt inputs and generated outputs (policy flag + deployment option). We can document the flags and how they are set in Dedicated/Private.
- Training: Redwood provides a contractual data-use opt-out: by default, customer data is not added to public model training pipelines without explicit opt-in. We will provide language for the contract ("data will not be used for model training or improvement").
- Data residency: We support region pinning; for hosted customers we can pin to US-East. For Dedicated/Private the data plane remains in customer-controlled VPC/region.
- KMS/BYOK: BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest for enterprise plans; role separation and audit trails are available.
- Access logs & audit: We retain and expose access logs (request id, timestamp, requester, model version, bytes in/out) in JSON format; default log retention is 12 months but can be shortened per contract. Logs can be exported to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Stackdriver).

Requested next steps:
1) I will share a short "Retention flags & how-to" doc and the draft SLA (attached).
2) Can you confirm a preferred window for logs (12 months default vs. shorter)?
3) Proposed security sync: 30-min on 6/16 or 6/17 with our Security Lead (Dev Patel). Please confirm SecOps availability.

If acceptable I’ll route a short statement on non-training language for legal to review and include in the SLA.

Thanks — looking forward to the SecOps sync.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: SLA-draft-Helix-2026.docx, redwood-prompt-data-flow.pdf
From: SecurityOps <sec-ops@helixmed.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@helixmed.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on prompt/output storage

Hi all — SecOps here. A few technical items we need clarified before the security sync: 

1) Exact retention controls and default values per deployment type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). Please indicate whether there are separate flags for: prompt_inputs, model_outputs, KV-cache, system logs.
2) For hosted: confirm that customer can request "0-day" retention for prompts/outputs and that Redwood will process the request within the SLA window (please state the timeframe).
3) Audit log schema: sample JSON with the top-level fields we can expect (request_id, timestamp_utc, user_id, model_version, bytes_in, bytes_out, data_residency_region).
4) Access controls: clarify RBAC model for Redwood employees and whether access to raw prompt text requires a privileged escalation/justification workflow.
5) Encryption: confirm envelope encryption and support for customer-provided keys (BYOK) for hosted enterprise customers; state whether keys are retained in Redwood KMS or passed through to customer KMS.

Please provide the above items as a short technical appendix ahead of the call. We need the appendix by EOD 2026-06-15 to meet Helix procurement timelines.

Thanks,
Helix Security Operations
sec-ops@helixmed.com
